questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

__
 
• The sentence expresses** a wish about a past action, indicating regret or a desire that something had not happened.**
 
• The word **"never"** is appropriate in this context as it correctly conveys the speaker's regret about coming to the place.
 
• Other options like **"right," "clear,"** and **"agreed" **do not fit the context of the sentence and do not convey the intended meaning of regret or wish.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *I wish we had **never** come here*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word** "never"** is often used in sentences that express a wish or regret about something that did not happen in the past.
 
• It is important to choose words that correctly convey the intended meaning and fit the grammatical structure of the sentence.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My daughter was / invited to lunch / hosted by the Governor / at his residence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the omission of the article "**a**" before the term "**lunch**."
 
• Singular countable nouns typically require an article ("a" or "an").
 
• The correct phrase should be "**to a lunch**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"My daughter was invited to a lunch hosted by the Governor at his residence."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "at his residence"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "hosted by the Governor"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "My daughter was"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The new software / consists from / several features / and tools.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the preposition 'from' is incorrect.
 
• The correct preposition to use with the verb **'consists' is 'of'.**
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the sentence should be 'consists of several features and tools'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *The new software **consists of** several features and tools*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The verb** 'consists'** should always be followed by the preposition** 'of'.**
 
• Using the incorrect preposition can lead to grammatical errors and confusion in meaning.
 
 
• **Example:** The committee **consists of** several members.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• The idiom 'easier said than done' means that something is easy to talk about but much more difficult to actually do.
 
• **This fits perfectly with the context of the sentence, which talks about the difficulty of starting to exercise every day despite it sounding easy.**
 
• **Idioms are a form of expression **that cannot be understood from the literal meanings of the words that make them up.
 
• They often add color and vivid imagery to **language, making it more engaging and expressive.**
 
• **Understanding the correct context **in which an idiom is used is crucial for its proper application.​
 
• Hence, the correct answer is 'option 2.'

Correct sentence: *It's easy to say that you'll start exercising every day, but it is **easier said than done**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Other options do not fit the context of the sentence:

 
• **Option 1: 'like fish out of water' **means being uncomfortable or out of place.
 
• **Option 3: 'crying wolf'** means raising a false alarm.
 
• **Option 4: 'going the extra mile'** means putting in extra effort.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

She has / bought / a car / two years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence uses the present perfect tense** 'She has bought',** which is incorrect when referring to a specific time in the past like **'two years ago'**.
 
• The present perfect tense is used to describe actions that have occurred at an unspecified time before now, whereas 'two years ago' specifies a definite time in the **past.**
 
• Therefore, the correct form should be the simple past tense** 'She bought' instead of 'She has bought'.**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: ***She bought a car two years ago*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The simple past tense is used for actions that were completed at a specific point in the **past.**
 
• Examples:
 
 
• *She finished her homework an hour ago.*
 
• *They moved to a new house last month.*
